task_instruction: Rewrite each affirmative statement as a negative question.
paragraphs: At 6:20 on Tuesday morning, the AI desk at the Meridian Ledger received a tip about a new language model from Meridian Labs. The tip claimed that the company had quietly begun an external evaluation weeks before its public announcement. {{red:Meridian Labs began externally testing the agent six weeks ago.}} {{mask_1}}? The first benchmark table seemed to support the claim. {{red:The agent scored above the benchmark's declared threshold.}} {{mask_2}}?

The desk's data editor, Imani, examined the methodology before anyone drafted a headline. The lab's technical note made a strong claim about the training data. {{red:The research team had excluded all synthetic examples from the evaluation set.}} {{mask_3}}? Meanwhile, the version circulating among reporters described an ongoing third-party review. {{red:The model is being assessed by an independent audit firm.}} {{mask_4}}? Imani called the auditors and asked whether they had checked the benchmark files themselves. Their written response was unusually specific. {{red:The audit firm has verified every item in the public test set.}} {{mask_5}}?

A second tip concerned the model's ability to recognize fabricated audio. The Ledger's science correspondent had tested a demonstration clip, but she wanted to know whether the result held up beyond the company's own material. {{red:The system can distinguish cloned voices from live callers.}} {{mask_6}}? A researcher at a university lab then sent over a replication note. {{red:A second lab replicated the result on consumer hardware.}} {{mask_7}}? The note included the device specifications, scripts, and failed runs, which made it more useful than the polished launch video.

At the same time, Imani checked the terms attached to the model release. The company's announcement promised downloadable weights, not just access through a hosted service. {{red:The company is releasing the model weights under a permissive license.}} {{mask_8}}? The license text appeared to allow commercial use, with attribution as its main condition. {{red:The license allows commercial redistribution.}} {{mask_9}}? The documentation history showed one late change to the safety section. {{red:The documentation was updated after the first draft.}} {{mask_10}}? The developers' repository also contained a folder of adversarial prompts. {{red:The developers have published the red-team prompts.}} {{mask_11}}?

The policy reporter, Tomas, traced a separate claim to a regulator's preliminary notice. The notice set out what a company would have to report after a serious incident, but it did not say that an investigation had begun. {{red:The regulator's preliminary notice requires an incident report within 72 hours.}} {{mask_12}}? A spokesperson said the startup had already responded to the notice. {{red:The startup has already filed that report.}} {{mask_13}}? When Tomas asked for the filing receipt, the spokesperson said the legal team was checking the numbers first. {{red:Its legal team is still reviewing the exposure estimates.}} {{mask_14}}?

By midafternoon, the newsroom had enough material for a careful story, but not enough to settle every question. The safety board had authority to pause the pilot if the evidence warranted it. {{red:The safety board could delay deployment pending further testing.}} {{mask_15}}? Meeting notes suggested that the board had seen an earlier evaluation before it approved the trial. {{red:The board had received the latest evaluation before approving the pilot.}} {{mask_16}}? A leaked memo, whose provenance remained uncertain, described a problem with the model's handling of private records. {{red:The leaked memo was written by an external contractor.}} {{mask_17}}? The company's spokesperson had addressed the leak in a short statement. {{red:A spokesperson has denied that the memo is authentic.}} {{mask_18}}?

Imani refused to publish the allegation as fact. She asked the team to separate what the documents established from what sources merely inferred, and to give the company a final chance to respond. The editor wanted to know whether their draft made that distinction clear. {{red:The story distinguishes verified findings from unconfirmed claims.}} {{mask_19}}? Before filing, Tomas checked the correction policy and the timestamp on every archived document. The editor read the final version once more. {{red:The story deserves a correction before publication.}} {{mask_20}}? They held the headline until the auditors confirmed that the public test set matched the version described in the report.
